articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Embedding Models for Keyword Extraction Using KeyBERT Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: KeyBERT is a method for keywords/keyphrases extraction, which has three steps. The first step is selecting candidate keywords from a text using sklearn library, the second step is the embedding operation of the text and its candidate keywords; this operation is done by BERT to get a numerical representation that represents the meanings. The third step is calculating the cosine similarity between individual keywords vectors and document vector. In this paper, we focus on the second step of KeyBERT (embedding step). Although KeyBERT has a lot of supported models for the embedding operation, there are no extensive previous comparative studies to analyze and study the effect of using different supported models in KeyBERT. We introduce a comparative study of two commonly used groups of models; the first group is sentence-transformers pretrained models, supported via the sentence-transformers library, and the second group includes the Longformer model, supported via the Hugginface Transformers library. We conduct the comparative study of models on benchmark datasets, which contain English text documents of multi-domains with different text lengths. Based on the study, we found that the Paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2 model provides the best results among all other models in keyword extraction in terms of effectiveness (f1-score, recall, precision, MAP) on all datasets, with higher efficiency (time) on short text compared with using it on long text; accordingly, we recommend using it in that context. On the other hand, the Longformer model is the most efficient/fastest in keyword extraction among all other models on all datasets and this superiority has been evident, especially in long text; accordingly, we recommend using it in that context.

articleTitle: Eye-to-Text Communication Based on Human-Computer Interface Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Eye-to-text communication is a technology that has gained significant importance in recent years in the field of human-computer interaction (HCI), becoming increasingly necessary for people with speech impairments or movement disabilities. Therefore, the webcam, Raspberry Pi 3, and display screen have been used to gather data from an eye’s movement in the left, right, top, bottom, and blink directions. This research aims to design a system that converts eye-to-text communication to preview the typing on the display screen in real-time, which is low-cost and non-invasive. The system utilizes OpenCV2, Dlib, Numpy, and Pandas libraries for data collection from a webcam and enables the extraction of values from user eye movements on the Excel sheet. The system suggested that two stages are needed to calculate the ratio. First stage: To detect eye blinking by the Dlib library, detect facial landmarks in the region of the eye, and then calculate the eye aspect ratio (EAR) between these landmarks. Second stage: By using the OpenCV2 library to convert the image into grayscale format, creating a black mask to detect the region of the eye only, calculating all white pixels on the left side and right side, and dividing the left pixels by the right pixels to get the ratio of pixels to select toward the eyes. According to our experience, the algorithms produced satisfying results when tested with an accuracy of 93.7% in real-time, including the Dlib algorithm with an accuracy of 94.5% and the OpenCV2 algorithm with an accuracy of 92.9%.

articleTitle: Abnormal Event Behavior Detection For Home Surveillance Cameras System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Home surveillance cameras have a crucial role in ensuring the security and safety of residential premises. However, analyzing the vast amount of video data generated by these cameras manually is a time-consuming and challenging task. This study designed a camera work system consisting of three main modules namely object detection, face recognition, and anomaly behavior to detecting abnormal event behavior. Object detection used the Histogram Oriented Gradient and Support Vector Machine (HOG-SVM) combination. Facial recognition used Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with the Visual Geometry Group-16 (VGG16) architecture that utilized transfer learning. Anomaly detection used spatiotemporal autoencoder based on threshold. Modules are tested using the standard metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and f1score. The three modules are integrated using a state machine into one system that can detect the abnormal event behavior. The overall accuracy of the system reached 84%, the precision value was 84.615%, the recall value was 94.286%, and the f1score was 89.189%.

articleTitle: Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePo4) Batteries Health Prognosis via Plateau Identification During High-Rate Charging and Discharging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The stability and performance of lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are significantly impacted by high-rate loading effects. The plateau voltage and capacity are a critical parameter when evaluating the performance, stability, and overall health of a battery, particularly in rechargeable Li-ion batteries. This paper focuses on a data-driven battery management system (BMS) approach for load-sensitive applications, such as battery energy storage systems (BESS) for electric vehicles (EVs) to ensure safe and stable performance during high-rate loading. It investigates the deterioration of lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) batteries, which are well-known for their high energy density and optimal performance at high temperature during charge-discharge loading variation above standard current-rate (C-rate). The paper proposes a plateau voltage and capacity identification model at different loading rates to accurately determine the degree of battery ageing in load-sensitive applications such as EV. In addition, the statistical linear regression (SLR) analysis model and the deep neural network (DNN) model are the proposed methods for identifying plateau voltage and capacity. It is found that at distinct loading rates, the DNN model outperforms the SLR model, which also functions exceptionally well with a maximum accuracy of 99.9%.

articleTitle: A 3D Board Game Using a Randomized Algorithm and AI to Improve English Vocabulary Retention and Fluency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: English’s dominance as the world’s most widely spoken language has shown how attractive it is to students looking to advance their education. Due to its dominance in business and education, English has become a prerequisite for many professions. Some primary barriers to speaking English clearly and fluently include a lack of inspiration and desire, the use of traditional learning and teaching techniques, being discouraged by teachers and instructors, and a fear of not learning English quickly. Using board games in English language training has been the focus of study, particularly in improving students’ speaking abilities, fluency, and accuracy. This study examines how a 3D mobile learning board game affects high school students’ vocabulary retention and fluency. The game was designed to supplement traditional teaching methodologies using game-based learning concepts. The researchers used an iterative approach to design, test, and enhance the board game application. The mobile game application was created using a randomized algorithm. The game’s effectiveness in enhancing pupils’ English language proficiency was also determined by reviewing survey data. According to the findings, employing the board game had a statistically significant beneficial effect and fit the ISO 9126 Evaluation. These findings imply that including board games in English language learning can augment instructional methodologies, raise student learning motivation, active involvement, and focus, and improve social skills, knowledge, and problem-solving abilities.

articleTitle: Modeling a Single Camera System based on Predicted Bounding Box and Pan-Tilt Angles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The control schemes that are related to visual servoing systems are often done through trial and error. Based on the classical control concept, it is necessary to have a mathematical model of the plant before designing the controller. Therefore, this research focuses on producing a mathematical model of the pan-tilt system. We propose the combination of the computer vision method with the classic system identification method, namely N4SID to obtain the dynamics model of a pan-tilt system. In this research, the system identification procedure was successful in producing a state-space model of a visual servoing system using a pan-tilt system and a single camera. This study merged traditional system identification techniques with computer vision to create a discrete-time linear state-space model. When the system order value equals three, the approximation with the minimum MSE value is obtained.

articleTitle: Quantifying Object-Oriented System Complexity: Introducing a Powerful Measurement Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: A lot of metrics and tools have been devised to measure the complexity of software systems. Through measurement, software professionals can have a better understanding and control of a software’s complexity. In this paper, we reviewed complexity metrics and tools for object-oriented systems. The existing tools measure either implemented systems which may be source code or compile binaries, or class diagrams. The tools that measure implemented systems already offer a wide variety of features to satisfy different needs. However, the tools that measure class diagrams are not only poor in amount, but all take in class diagram XMI files, with none of them taking in PlantUML class diagram source code. PlantUML is a popular text-based UML diagramming tool that enables users to define UML diagrams with a domain specific language then renders the diagram for them. Hence, we developed a web application that measures class diagram complexity via PlantUML class diagram source code. It measures five class metrics and seven system metrics visualized as tables and bar charts, with the results exportable to PDF and CSV. Our tool’s measurements were also evaluated to be correct when it is within our scope of supported syntax.

articleTitle: SDA Plus: Improving the Performance of the System Determine Algorithm (SDA) of the Switching Between AES-128 and AES-256 (MOLAZ Method)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: There are many encryption algorithms; some of them are strong but slow in decryption, unlike other methods. The MOLAZ method is one of the encryption techniques in UUM’s thesis - 2010 used to improve the difficulty of protecting information while preserving the speed of encryption and decryption. This approach involves alternating utilization of two algorithms, AES-128 and AES256, to integrate them within the encryption procedure of a single plain text. The MOLAZ method depends on the SDA algorithm to organize all operations of the encryption/decryption. However, the biggest challenge is that SDA performs the segmentation, distribution, and aggregation operations sequentially, making the time loss cost significant, especially if the data volume is enormous. In this study, The SDA was developed and usually designed to segment the system's work in parallel, where the time and complexity of encryption are shortened by the MOLAZ method. The system generates sub-systems that operate independently without referring to the central system. In particular, saving hardware resources while implementing 256-bit AES and 128-bit AES modules is made possible by reducing the processing time. Most of the modules created can be used for AES encryption and decryption. Besides, the architecture will also provide a fast data rate in encoding and decoding. So, take advantage of the power of AES-265 and the speed of AES-128 in the presence of big data; that is why developed SDA. The proposed architecture is ideal for applications critical to encrypting and decrypting massive data in the hard disk etc.

articleTitle: ROADWISE: Infrastructure Design Evaluation and Reporting System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Road infrastructure development and maintenance are crucial for economic growth and public safety. A web-based application for the Road Infrastructure Design Evaluation and Reporting System (ROADWISE) has been developed to streamline these operations. This innovative system uses digital technologies to improve the efficiency and efficacy of road infrastructure management. ROADWISE is a web application utilizing a trained machine-learning model to report and evaluate road quality. It also examines road width, signage, intersections, sidewalks, and pedestrian bike lanes. Likewise, the researchers evaluate the successful integration of Yolo into the ROADWISE machine-learning system. This integration has proven highly effective in monitoring possible road improvements and reducing traffic accidents. System performance assessment and evaluation were conducted using Google Forms survey questionnaires with the ISO/IEC 9126 standard criteria and analyzed by a diverse group, including IT professionals, road users, and students. The result gave an average rating of 5.28 out of 6.00, indicating agreement with the system’s effectiveness. In summary, the web-based Road Infrastructure Design Evaluation and Reporting System application represents a significant advancement in infrastructure management. It harnesses the power of technology to streamline processes, enhance transparency, and contribute to the development of safe and efficient road networks.

articleTitle: Investigation of Single Segment Side-Polished Optical Fiber Sensor for Shoulder Joint Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Shoulder monitoring is an important stage in the diagnosis and treatment process of affected patients. Current devices available in the clinical environment for this application are focusing on flexible ruler or manual goniometer, which are prone to measurement error. Alternative approaches including accelerometer, magnetometer, strain sensor and inertial measurement unit (IMU) are subject to reading error, susceptible to output drift, has bulky overall size and difficult to be attached on the human body (via adhesive or garment). To solve this issue, this paper presents the use of an optical fiber sensor (OFS) based on intensity modulation technique via single segment side-polished fiber. Based on the experimental study, the proposed method can be utilized to measure an angle between 0deg. and 90 deg. Additional optical sensors can be added to increase the sensor’s range of motion that is sufficient for shoulder joint measurement.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Automated Retrieval of Fuel Price Data from Captured Images at Gas Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Fuel price fluctuations, including both increases and decreases, are a common occurrence when it comes to driving a vehicle. The Waze navigation application provides a platform for users to input and share fuel prices through crowd-sourced data manually. In a recent research study, an automated approach was developed to supply accurate fuel price information. This approach involved training a Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) to recognize fuel-related signs, and Google’s Cloud Vision API was employed for Optical Character Recognition (OCR). These technologies collectively offered an efficient means for users to contribute to and access crowd-sourced fuel price details. A web application was created to extract fuel prices from these signs, achieving a notable Mean Average Precision (mAP) score of 66.6% through the trained SSD model. Through user evaluations, the research demonstrated a mean average satisfaction score of 4.6, indicating alignment with ISO 25010 and 25012 standards encompassing functional suitability, performance efficiency, and accuracy. The research study effectively designed a web-based solution that proficiently extracts fuel prices from images of fuel station price boards using a combination of object detection and OCR.

articleTitle: Hydroponic System for Effective Microplastic Filtration in the Sea: A Revolutionary Low-Cost Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The Low-Cost Microplastic Filtration System is a device designed to aid in the resolution of the growing problem with microplastics. With an estimated 48 million shopping bags and 164 million sachets used daily (Philippine research uncovers microplastics inside a regularly eaten fish, 2020), the Philippines is one of the most prolific users of single-use plastics. This plastic garbage winds up in the oceans due to the country’s still-developing waste management infrastructure, making it the third-largest source of marine plastic pollution. To demonstrate the existence of microplastics in the sea in Brgy. Papaya Nasugbu, Batangas, the researchers collected water samples from the targeted area and isolated the particles from the water. Using a hot needle method, the collected particles were tested for microplastics. If a suspected particle bends or rips while in contact with the heated needle, it is classified as a microplastic. The water sample was subsequently purified using the project’s filtration equipment. The water sample was found to be clean, with no visible particulates. The system uses filtered seawater to irrigate the plants that are incorporated into the system. Coriander, the plant employed in the study, also showed signs of development after being introduced into the system.

articleTitle: Meander-Line Slots Based Miniaturized Inset-Fed Patch-Sensor Antenna for Water Characterization Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This article presents a miniaturized size Microstrip-patch sensor structure based on meander-line slot for water-quality and salinity measurement applications. The HFSS-software tool is employed to design and simulate the proposed sensor. The proposed sensor is printed on $60\times 50\times 1~mm^{3}$ a dielectric material of FR-4 type. The meander-line slot resonator is inserted in the patch-sensor for miniaturize with the sensitivity enhancement. In order to contain the water sample that wants to be tested, a receptacle with dimensions of $47.75\times 50\times 4~mm^{3}$ is mounted on the sensor structure. The receptacle is made from PTFE-Teflon dielectric material. The miniaturize sensor is noticed resonant at 2.74 GHz for unloaded-state. Furthermore, it’s found resonant at; 2.44 GHz, 2.49 GHz, and 2.5 GHz for DI-water, fresh-water and sea-water respectfully. The miniaturized-sensor is showed good sensing values that equals to 0.901 for DI-water, 0.751 for fresh-water, and 0.721 for Sea-water. Finally, a good agreement is showed between the measurement results and those from simulation.

articleTitle: Patterning of Monolithic Integrated Circuit using Electron Beam Lithography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: This paper presents the technique and procedures of fabricating micro sized monolithic integrated circuit (MIC) using electron beam lithography (EBL). In order to realize a small circuit sizes device by EBL, several steps need to be carried out. These include sample cleaning, resist coating, pattern generation, initial beam focus and stigmation correction, sample calibration, write-field calibration, re-correction of beam focus and stigmation condition, pattern exposure and development process. It was found that a narrow transmission line of $0.6 \mu \mathrm{m}$ width can be obtained by EBL process using the following exposure parameters; 20 keV acceleration voltage, 0.15 nA beam current and 150 m As/cm$^{2}$ exposure dosage with a dose factor of three and write field magnification of $\times 150$.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Syringe Pumping Using Smart Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The process of infusion of medication automatically is one of the modern methods of giving treatment to patients. The pumping system for the drug is being developed using Raspberry Pi to control the amount of pumping with three syringes and the possibility of controlling it at a specific time, as well as a pumping speed can be controlled. The system is designed by a 3d printer and programmed in Python language with multiple SPO2, and Temperature sensors to offer a high sensitivity to detect any changes in the health status of the human body. The goal of designing and implementing a multi-channel syringe pump is to reduce errors caused by the manual injection of drugs and the mixing of accurate quantities. Also works to organize the treatment after reading the vital activities of the body through the sensors in the proposed device. The developed system is portable, versatile, and reasonably priced.

articleTitle: Rollover Stability Control of Autonomous Forklift Using Optimal Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: E-commerce and the industrial revolution have impacted the warehousing system. The warehousing system is continuously developing into modern warehousing. One of the features of a modern warehousing system is a forklift that can operate independently or automatically. Autonomous forklifts have a broad scope. This study presents the roll stability control of autonomous forklifts. The roll stability control is necessary to avoid instability that can cause rollover. The center of gravity is one of the crucial factors in anticipating rollover. The center of gravity can be affected by the weight of the load and the speed at which the forklift operates. The forklift dynamic model is developed here by considering the calculated center of gravity and the lateral transfer ratio (LTR). A linear quadratic regulator (LQR) and model predictive control (MPC) are then employed to stabilize and regulate the LTR at zero. The simulation results of a case study show that LQR and MPC may avoid rollover with a relatively fast response when the forklift has half loads and slow movements.

articleTitle: Tuning of Fractional Order PD for Position Servo System Using FOMCON
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: In this study, a position servo was controlled using a fractional-order PD controller. In comparison to its integer-order counterpart, fractional-order control was known to offer higher performance and stability. However, fractional-order PD requires tuning for more parameters, making design more challenging. The availability of numerous tuning platforms today makes the use of FOPD more practical. In this work, the FOPD was tuned using FOMCON toolbox which offers numerous optimization technique to choose from. This study examined the outcome from using Nelder-Mead, Interior point, SQP, and Active-Set optimization techniques in tuning the FOPD while minimizing the ISE criteria. In this study, initial value of FOPD was randomly set to 0.1, 0.01 and 0.5 for the Kp, Kd and $\mu$ respectively. The parameters turned out quite differently with the output from Interior-point technique seems to be the fastest compared to the rest.

articleTitle: LabVIEW-based Design of Smart Wireless Monitoring System for Cardiac Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: In recent decades, heart disease has emerged as a major threat to public health. The challenge problem in such diseases is to diagnose the problems in the heart early before get a critical threat in human’s life. In this study, ECG surveillance system has been designed and implemented in real-time environment to detect and diagnose the heart disease with low cost and burden on patients. The real-time implementation of the device includes both hardware and software designs. The medical device AD8232 will record the patient’s electrocardiogram (ECG) from the chest and transmit these data to a PC computer via Arduino DUE. Then, the ECG data will be sent to LabVIEW programming platform to make usual medical analysis. Inside LabVIEW platform, the features of ECG features are extracted using wave transform. Subsequently, the results of analysis will be sent to IOT, where it is received by the Thing Speak server, from where it can be accessed by a doctor or hospital via a mobile device for diagnosis.

articleTitle: ZigBee Wireless Sensor Network-based Irrigation System for Small-Scale Farm Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Managing water resources for agricultural purposes is becoming increasingly complex due to the scarcity of fresh water on a global scale. Therefore, the wireless sensor network (WSN) has been used to monitor the fields and gather information about conditions such as soil moisture and weather conditions. This research aims to design and implement a WSN for water management irrigation systems in small-scale farm fields. The system consists of five nodes. One coordinator node and four sensor nodes. Each sensor node consists of soil moisture, air temperature, and humidity sensors to monitor the conditions in the agriculture field. An Arduino Nano ATmega328P microcontroller processes the data from these sensors and sends it via XBee S2C to the coordinator node to be monitored by the laptop for the control opening or closing of the water pump. Moreover, the data is stored on the laptop for later use in smart irrigation systems based on the artificial intelligence algorithm.

articleTitle: Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Object detection in self-driving cars is a prime component because there is no human control over the cars’ driving. Self-driving cars must detect an object 360 degrees around the car for the car to steer or handle the driving on the correct track. The market for autonomous vehicles is rapidly growing, and as all people now know about the level of technology in the developed countries, which are the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, England, and Japan, those countries are going all out in the creation of electric and autonomous vehicles. However, most of the current object detection methods are expensive and ineffective. Therefore, in this paper, the new, efficient, and faster design of object detection in autonomous vehicles using the YOLOv5 neural network is investigated, explored, designed, implemented, and evaluated. YOLOv5 is the best model because it is built on the Python framework, is available in a variety of sizes, and is constantly updated and improved. The Python platform, Roboflow tool, and Google Colab were adopted to design the model. Roboflow is great for object detection because of smart polygons, label assist, commenting, and exporting in a variety of formats. Meanwhile, Google Colab is free to use (allows you to run Python code in the cloud), easy to use (user-friendly interface), and offers access to powerful GPUs. The adoption of these with the YOLOv5 neural network is a new attempt in autonomous vehicles. As a result, a better and more efficient object detection method yet affordable for autonomous vehicles was produced and is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Passive Harmonic Compensator-based System for Analyzing and Mitigating Harmonic Distortion in a 34.5 kV Electrical System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Traditional power quality analysis is time-consuming, expensive, and prone to human error. Several techniques and approaches exist for reading, analyzing, and monitoring power quality, involving computations, algorithms, software, or a combination of both. Despite the variety of Power Quality Analyzers available, no software combines analysis and recommendations into one application. This paper designed software that analyzes power quality data to identify and address harmonic distortions. The goal is to recommend passive filter sizing to reduce harmonic distortions, and downtime, and ensure compliance with regulations. The software, limited to the client's data, successfully reduced total harmonic distortion (THD) to less than 1% for the 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonic orders. The software system is a highly effective tool for reducing THD and improving power quality. It has an accuracy of more than 95%, the effectiveness of remodeled filters than the existing is more than 90 percent and can be used to target specific harmonic distortion orders. The remodeled filter recommendation is particularly effective, achieving significant reductions in target harmonic distortion by Philippine Distribution Code 3.2.4.4 of 2017. Future researchers are encouraged to include waveforms in the software for graphical representation, enhance credibility through real-world case studies and benchmark systems, result in interpretations, and filter sizing guidelines for improved usability and reliability.

articleTitle: Child Car Seat Alert System via Load and Temperature Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The paper presents the development of a safety feature system for children car seat installation against potential involuntary child abandonment in vehicles. Motivation of current work was derived from persistent issues that resulted in the death of infants, which was left inside a car by their oblivious parents. To arrive at this objective, a system comprises of load cell, temperature sensor, buzzer and a microcontroller was developed to perform a coherent system to alert the parents when an infant was detected in the child car seat while the engine was turned off and temperature build-up was detected inside the vehicle. Result from testing indicate that the developed system is triggered in accordance with the set range of above 3.5 kg and 35-degree Celsius.

articleTitle: Proposed Electrical Stimulation Device for Wound Healing Therapy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The management of chronic wounds has emerged as a crucial and significant concern for patients afflicted with chronic diseases like diabetic foot disease. This condition has escalated into a life-threatening issue for numerous individuals worldwide. Electrical stimulation devices have played a pivotal role in addressing various cases and have had a direct impact on the advancement of therapeutic techniques and healthcare in the domain of wound treatment and healing. Design an Electrical Stimulation ES device facing many challenges suck as the compellability of the device, how to design ES device able to provide many therapeutic techniques with high efficiency and low cost. This paper presents a proposed electrical stimulation device, which has been designed utilizing the Arduino platform's Integrated Development Environment IDE and fritzing. The proposed model in this research paper offers characteristics such as current, voltage, and variable frequencies. It applies to numerous medical conditions and diverse types of wounds, be they acute or chronic. The Electrical Stimulation ES device in this study delivers a direct or monophasic current signal with varying strengths and adjustable periods, which contribute to the healing process. To assess the efficacy of the electrical stimulation device, both the Direct Current Mode DCM and the Monophasic Current Mode MPCM were tested on whole blood WB samples using an in vitro method. The vitro results show that the Direct current mode provide the best effect on the blood sample during the testing of the proposed Electrical stimulation device on patients that suffer or not suffer from diabetic foot disease.

articleTitle: Impact of Climate Variability on Oil Palm Yield
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Oil palm yield is a crucial aspect in determining the profitability of the worldwide oil palm sector. The amount of oil that can be extracted from an oil palm plantation is dependent on a variety of factors, the most important of which is the climate condition. The amount of oil palm that can be harvested is significantly affected by climate. Oil palm trees produce the most fruit when they are grown in regions that are both warm and humid. In addition, for optimal growth, oil palm trees need to be planted in soil that drains well. The tree will not be able to form strong roots if the soil is too heavy or too damp, and as a result, it will produce a lower amount of fruit. The purpose of this article is to investigate the climate elements that will have a significant impact on oil palm productivity. Data was collected from the years 2020 until 2022. The research conducted an analysis and found that there was a consistent multiple R value over 0.7 for three consecutive years. Additionally, the R square value was determined to be 0.62 in 2020, 0.546 in 2021, and 2022. The correlation analysis indicates a significant relationship between temperature, wind speed, humidity, and oil palm production. However, no significant correlation was observed between rainfall and oil palm yield.

articleTitle: Facilitating Comprehension: An NLP-Based Converter for 7th Grade Students to Transform English Sentences into Mathematical Expressions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Based on research findings, a significant obstacle for students in learning mathematics is their difficulty understanding word problems. Converting verbal explanations into mathematical equations becomes difficult, especially when several procedures are necessary. Thus, this study developed a supplemental tool for grade 7 students that is designed to assist them in effectively converting English language phrases into mathematical expressions, thereby enhancing their learning experience. This study encompasses both a web application and a translation algorithm. The web application is an educational tool that delivers content that teaches the mathematical concept of “Translating English Phrases and Sentences into Mathematical Equations and Statements”. Meanwhile, the translation algorithm, developed using Stanza, a Python Natural Language Processing (NLP) package, is tasked with transforming given English mathematical phrases into their corresponding mathematical expressions. The system was created using the Rapid Application Development (RAD) software development model to implement progressive improvements within three development iterations, and it was then assessed for functional suitability, usability, and reliability using the ISO/IEC-25010 System and software quality model. The outcomes of the survey evaluation revealed that the system proved to be fitting for learning math phrase translations. It proved dependability, convenience, and usability. Furthermore, the algorithm’s precision was evaluated, with 175 predictions yielding an accuracy rate of 81.14%. In summary, this study introduces a valuable resource for math educators and learners, enhancing their comprehension of math phrase translations.

articleTitle: Investigating the Performance of Thermal Comfort Prediction Model with Isolation Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: In the realm of human-environment interactions, thermal comfort plays a crucial role in influencing human activity. This sensation, representing an ideal balance where an individual feels neither too hot nor too cold in their thermal surroundings, is termed as ‘thermal comfort’. Given its subjective nature, thermal comfort varies significantly between individuals based on personal preferences. It is essential to note that this ambiguity does not arise from data noise or collection errors but stems from the inherent individuality in thermal comfort perceptions. Recent advancements have seen the adoption of machine learning techniques to forecast thermal comfort, but the performance is moderate. In this study, the Isolation Forest algorithm is leveraged to identify and eliminate ambiguous data from the ASHRAE thermal comfort dataset. A key hyperparameter of Isolation Forest is the contamination value, which is variably set at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 to investigate its effect on the prediction model’s performance. Following the data refinement using Isolation Forest, the prediction model is developed using Random Forest. Our results exhibit a notable improvement in the performance of the thermal comfort prediction model.

articleTitle: Neural Network based Covid-19 Diagnosis using X-ray and CT Scan Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Covid-19 is a lung disease that has recently spread widely worldwide. Therefore, machine learning was used in patient health care and early disease detection before the patient’s condition worsened. In this research, we used two data sets: the first group is represented by X-ray medical images, and ct images represent the second group. For each group, 250 RGB medical images of Covid-19, using the developed artificial neural networks (ANN) algorithm, are trained on image data to verify and test them. Moreover, we compared the two groups of medical images, X-ray and CT, with 15 neurons. Our results showed that the ANN performed exceptionally well. Performance indicators, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and accuracy, were 99.8% for the first group and 100% for the second group. Moreover, our method outperformed previous machine learning models.

articleTitle: DigiSign: A Mobile Application for Comparing Digitized Signature Using Feature Detection and Matching Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: A signature is a formal declaration of a person’s legal identity but can be copied and forged by others. Fake signatures in online transactions, including shipping, purchasing, and banking, can result in financial losses. This study examines how digitized signatures comparing systems work on touchscreen-based mobile devices. DigiSign is a mobile application designed to detect and match digitized signatures to determine whether they are similar or not. The application employs an image processing algorithm to transform digitized signatures into images, enabling the detection of keypoints through feature detection and matching to assess their similarities. By utilizing feature detection and feature matching to recognize keypoints, DigiSign ensures secure data storage in image memory or RAM, avoiding the need for storing sensitive information in databases. DigiSign utilized the BRISK algorithm and the hamming distance algorithm, resulting in a 38% acceptance rate for similarity. The application’s performance was evaluated according to ISO/IEC 25010 standards, achieving a mean score of 4.26 out of 5.0. The study confirms its effectiveness in accurately interpreting the resemblance of digital signatures, as indicated by the strongly agreed responses.

articleTitle: Descriptive Analysis on Data of Stingless Bee IoT Application Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: An Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring system for stingless bee farming provides a technologically advanced and data-driven approach to beekeeping, supporting sustainable agricultural practices while promoting the wellbeing of the bee colonies and increasing honey production. An IoT system frequently consists of numerous sensors that collect data in various aspects. Lack of data descriptive analysis especially on stingless bee farming characteristics shows some shortage of good results in forecasting stingless bee colonies for honey production. This paper presents a descriptive analysis and correlation coefficient of the data collected from live stingless bee IoT monitoring system. The data was taken at the Stingless Bee Research Centre at one of the university campuses in Malaysia. Four sensor devices were used to measure air temperature, humidity, weight and gas. Sample data from all sensors was taken within 29 days from May 11 to June 8, 2022 and was analyzed. The result presents detailed calculated descriptive analysis and correlation coefficient for all data sensors. The best correlation among the variables in the dataset is between temperature and humidity which is at negative 0.7378 that indicates a moderate negative correlation. Analysis found that the most active of stingless bees’ time is at 6. 59am to 8.20 am which at temperature 22°C that produced more honey. This research is significant in identifying the stingless bee habitats in forecasting honey production.

articleTitle: Using Hybrid GA/PSO-Mobile Sink to Improve Energy Efficiency and Network Lifetime for LEACH Protocol in WSNs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Utilising a hybrid Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) strategy in conjunction with a mobile sink, this study proposes a new approach for improving energy efficiency and extending the network lifetime in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This work is founded on the Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH) protocol. The conventional use of static sink nodes frequently results in an energy imbalance among sensor nodes, especially those close to the sink, leading to the premature exhaustion of their energy reserves. To combat this difficulty, a mobile sink framework is proposed, accompanied by a hybrid optimization strategy. Utilizing the Genetic Algorithm (GA), the optimal Cluster Heads (CHs) for the mobile sink’s trajectory are determined. If the optimal path cannot be determined, the PSO phase selects Collector Points for the mobile sink. Afterward, the optimal route between these sites is computed, and the superior route is selected for the ongoing cycle. The proposed hybrid GA/PSO-mobile sink strategy is contrasted to conventional WSN protocols through extensive simulation and performance evaluation. The results demonstrate significant improvements in energy efficiency and network lifetime, validating the approach’s efficacy in extending the operational lifetime of WSNs under the LEACH protocol while maintaining efficient data aggregation and communication.

articleTitle: A Review of Potential AI-Based Automation for IoT-Enabled Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has brought significant changes in the way we interact with technology in our homes. Smart homes equipped with IoT devices offer a comfortable and convenient lifestyle. However, managing these devices and their operations can be challenging, especially for individuals with limited technical expertise. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in IoT-based smart homes can potentially overcome these challenges by automating device management and enabling proactive responses to users’ needs. This paper investigates the potential of AI-based automation for IoT-enabled smart homes. We review the literature on AI-based automation and IoT-based smart homes, highlighting their benefits, challenges, and existing solutions. The research methodology used in this study is through deep learning approach. The results indicates that AI-based automation can improve user experience and enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of IoT-based smart homes. However, some technical and ethical challenges, such as privacy and security concerns, need to be addressed.

articleTitle: Bot or Human? Detection of DeepFake Text with Semantic, Emoji, Sentiment and Linguistic Features
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Detecting machine-generated text (MGT), also known as Deepfake text, has become increasingly important in Artificial Intelligence (AI) age and social media platforms. With the proliferation of MGT and the potential consequences of its dissemination, there is a pressing need to develop effective methods for distinguishing between MGT and human-written text (HWT). Our research aim has two-fold: firstly, to examine the inherent differences between MGT and HWT on Twitter, and secondly, to develop a classifier specifically designed for MGT detection on the platform. This classifier utilizes contextualized text embeddings as its foundation while considering additional linguistic features, sentiment features, and emoji embeddings. Our experimental results demonstrate that incorporating additional features enhances the model's ability to detect MGT. Combining fine-tuned BERT embeddings with emoji and linguistic features using a multi-layer perceptron classifier achieves the highest accuracy rate of 88.3%. Our analysis reveals distinct characteristics of MGT compared to HWT, including differences in engagement behavior, linguistic patterns, named entities, sentiment expressions, and text perplexity. Our research contributes to the field of MGT detection by offering a comprehensive approach that combines semantic text embeddings with supplementary features. The proposed model provides a significant step forward in addressing the challenge of Deepfake text detection.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Particle Swarm Optimisation Control for Traffic Light Systems in Roundabouts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Although the usage of roundabouts has been widely implemented as an alternative to signalised intersections as a version of traffic control, it is still reported that major traffic congestions commonly occur at roundabouts in urban areas. However, studies show that one of the most promising methods to overcome this issue is through the implementation of an evolutionary algorithm as a method to control the phase timings of the traffic light system at roundabouts. As such, this project aims to evaluate the effectiveness of implementing particle swarm optimisation (PSO) as the traffic light control for a signalised roundabout. Hence the performance of the PSO-controlled signalised roundabout is compared with that of a fixed-time signalised roundabout and also the unsignalised roundabout under different traffic conditions. This project presents a case study inspired by a real-world roundabout, namely the Persiaran Anggerik Mokara Roundabout in Kota Kemuning, Shah Alam, Malaysia. From the study, we can conclude that the usage of a Particle Swarm optimisation (PSO) algorithm is suitable in finding more effective green traffic light phase timings compared to fixed-time traffic lights for all test cases. However, the implementation of the PSO-controlled signalised roundabout is less effective compared to unsignalised roundabouts due the minimal delay incurred from an unsignalised round design. As such, it was concluded that when designing a roundabout system that is of similar characteristics as the modelled roundabout for this project, an unsignalised approach to the roundabout system greatly outperforms any traffic light system that only has traffic signals at the entrances of the roundabout.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection Using Social Media User Network and Engagement Features
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Today, social media has become a key source of news consumption, posing a crucial issue of disseminating and propagating a large volume of fake news. As manual fact-checking techniques are slow and time-consuming, automated fake news detection models that can efficiently manage vast volumes of information must be developed. While natural language processing and computational linguistics have been widely employed in previous research, they often prove inadequate for constructing robust models. By examining the behavior of social media users, this research incorporated user network and engagement features to capture the patterns of fake news propagation on social media. We aimed to examine these features from the understanding that users are influenced by social validation and homophily, which play a significant role in shaping their behavior within online social networks. These features are then incorporated into our proposed fake news detection model. Our experimental results have demonstrated the significance of these features, suggesting their usefulness and relevant effects in fake news detection. Overall, this research contributes to the ongoing efforts in combatting fake news by proposing and assessing the significance of user network and engagement features within a fake news detection framework.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Speed Prediction for Saudi Arabia via 1D-CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: As fluctuating wind power is incorporated into the energy mix, grid operators encounter dire challenges. Managing grid operations requires accurate knowledge of available wind power and its variation with time. Wind power can be estimated by providing reliable and fast wind speed prediction at different hub heights. Hence, this study proposes a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) model for wind speed prediction at different heights and aboveground levels (AGL). The results of the proposed model are compared with three deep learning models to validate its repeatability. The results show a competitive performance between the proposed model and the gated recurrent unit (GRU) network. Furthermore, the study indicates that capturing wind speed at 18m height for training is sufficient for predicting wind speed at higher elevations. Further research could focus on adding exogenous variables to assess their impact on predicting wind speed at different AGL heights.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Harris Hawks Optimization Algorithm in ANN Training Applied to Electricity Consumption Prediction in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Electricity consumption has been increasing over the past century and is expected to continue increasing soon. Predicting electricity consumption has thus been a topic of interest. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are reliable methods to be used as prediction models. However, as standalone models, they often have low accuracy. Hence optimizers including swarm intelligence algorithms are used for improving the models. In this paper, a recently introduced swarm intelligence algorithm, namely Harris Hawks optimization (HHO) has been employed for optimizing an ANN for the prediction of electricity consumption. Specifically, HHO is used as a training algorithm to get the best connection weights and biases of the ANN. The experimental results prove the effectiveness of HHO in optimizing the prediction model. In addition to HHO, two more recent and high-performing swarm intelligence algorithms, namely Dragonfly Algorithm (DA) and Whale optimization Algorithm (WOA) are also employed for optimizing the ANN. The performance of the prediction models optimized by HHO, DA, and WOA are evaluated by comparison of the root mean square error of the ANNs during the training and testing, the percentage decrease in RMSE from the initial to the final iterations during the training and the time taken for the algorithm to converge.

articleTitle: An Advanced Rivest Cipher 4 Algorithm to Transfer Fast and Secure Data Using Li-Fi Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The Light-Fidelity (Li-Fi) is a wireless communication technology that is light-based and can complete wireless fidelity (Wi-Fi) technologies for many applications. Li-Fi technology which uses light spectrum is a technology for solving the lack of radio spectrum at Wi-Fi. One of the main benefits of Li-Fi technology is the ability to communicate by light with a high level of safety. However, the signal of Li-Fi technology is the same as other signals that are susceptible to eavesdropping because no security system is infallible. The objective of this paper is to decrease the computational cost of encryption and decryption and keep the security of transformed data when transmitted via Li-Fi technology. This study proposes the advanced Rivest Cipher 4 (ARC4) algorithm that will be used in the physical layer of Li-Fi applications. The novelty will be in the pseudo-random generation algorithm (PRGA) which is part of Rivest Cipher 4 (RC4). The data will become an index of the s-array and get the value of that index in the s-array instead of using the XOR operation. The proposed ARC4 was evaluated by the National Institute of Science and Technology (NIST) test. The obtained results illustrate that ARC4 is more robust and effective than RC4 when the data is transformed by Li-Fi communication.

articleTitle: Sustainable Electrification Scheme in Nijhum Dwip: A Pre-Feasibility Study of Hybrid Renewable Energy Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The article investigates the potential of various renewable energy technologies on Nijhum Dwip, an island located in the Bay of Bengal. Due to the island’s completely isolated location in the sea, there is acute unavailability of transmission lines and modern amenities which made this site an ideal candidate where renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, hydrokinetic and biomass energy should be introduced in order to reduce its carbon footprint to nearly zero. Using the HOMER software, different setups of hybrid renewable energy systems were optimized based on system sizes, combinations of renewable energy sources and other factors. The results showed that the combination of solar panels, wind turbines, and hydrokinetic systems is the most cost-effective and sustainable option for Nijhum Dwip. The total NPC for this hybrid energy system was only ${\$}$5,158,250.00 with an impressive COE of ${\$}$0.4291 which is quite reasonable in terms of the hybrid system being absolutely clean which in return preserves the bio-diversity of the island. The article concludes by highlighting the potential of Nijhum Dwip to serve as a model for other small islands and remote communities seeking sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Transforming Tannery Waste into Biogas: An Exploration of Biogas Production via Anaerobic Digestion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: On an annual basis, approximately 86,000 metric tons of raw skins and hides are processed in Bangladesh to produce leather. The operations of tanneries yield substantial volumes of both solid and liquid waste. The application of waste stabilization through anaerobic digestion (AD) presents an opportunity to generate biogas, thereby establishing a sustainable energy source. This study was conducted with the primary objective of assessing the feasibility of employing anaerobic digestion for the management of solid waste generated by tanneries (referred to as TSW) during the initial stages of tanning. Furthermore, the investigation aimed to draw a comparison between the effects of TSW and cow dung when used as substrates. Through the amalgamation of tannery solid waste (TSW) with diverse substrates, the process of biogas production was initiated on the fourth day of the reaction and has consistently increased thereafter. Each experimental reactor exhibited a distinct cumulative gas production rate, dependent on the variations in the proportions of tannery solid waste, poultry droppings, and cow dung. This study showcases a TSW anaerobic digestion technique that achieves an optimal carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio along with a high concentration of volatile solids (VS) by blending with different substrates. The removal rates of chemical oxygen demand (COD) were recorded as follows for the series of five reactors (R$_{A}$, R$_{B}$, R$_{C}$, R$_{D}$, and R$_{E}$): 49.22%, 51.77%, 47.70%, 46.88%, and 48.12%, respectively. Notably, reactor R$_{B}$, which exhibited the highest gas production, also achieved the most substantial COD removal among the reactors.

articleTitle: Predicting Intention to Recommend Digital Citizen Participation using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Digital citizen participation uses innovative technologies to enable, engage, and empower citizens to communicate with the government on different needs, concerns, and challenges. To this date, limited studies explain the intention and recommendation for digital citizen participation, particularly from the Philippines. Thus, this study aims to understand digital citizen participation through a survey that examines factors on the intention to use and recommend digital citizen participation among Filipino citizens. A conceptual model was developed based on trust, technology acceptance, and empowerment theory. The framework relationships were tested using machine learning algorithms. The results show that perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, trust, and empowerment theory positively predicted the intention to recommend digital citizen participation. Furthermore, this study indicates that Filipinos have positive intention and are willing to recommend digital citizen participation. Finally, this work provides evidence of the explanatory power of the conceptual model through machine learning models on digital citizen participation. This work presents some important research and practical implications in digital citizen participation.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Data Fusion and Machine Learning for Vehicle Manoeuvre Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Vehicle manoeuvre analysis is vital for road safety as it helps understand driver behaviour, traffic flow, and road conditions. However, classifying data from in-vehicle acquisition systems or simulators for manoeuvre recognition is complex, requiring data fusion and machine learning (ML) algorithms. This paper proposes a hybrid approach that combines multivariate multiscale entropy (MMSE) and one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs). MMSE is utilised for early feature extraction and data fusion, and the extracted features are classified using 1D-CNNs, achieving an impressive 87% test accuracy in multiclass classification. This paper provides insights into improving vehicle manoeuvre classification using advanced ML techniques and data fusion methods to handle complex data sets effectively. Ultimately, this approach can enhance the understanding of driver behaviour, inform policy decisions, and develop more effective strategies to enhance road safety.

articleTitle: Sitting Posture Notification and Monitoring System: A sensor application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Improper sitting posture is a common issue affecting many individuals, even young ones. Prolonged periods of sitting, whether at work, studying, or at home, can lead to back pain and other health problems. The study focused on the software’s material specifications and system flow required to create the system. The engineering design process involved using real-time image processing and force-sensitive resistors to determine the posture of the user. The human pose estimation method was used to estimate the body model parameters. The study found that familiarity with different hardware and software is important to create the project easily. The force-sensitive resistor provided high-accuracy results, but factors such as distortion can affect the outcome when using the camera. The mathematical model created by the researchers produced accurate results. The system helps users maintain proper sitting posture and monitor their improper sitting behavior history and records. Future research could consider the use of other components for more reliable use and delve into the safety of the different components used. Improvements to the camera holder, position, and power source could also enhance project efficiency. Overall, the development of a sitting posture notification and monitoring system can aid in preventing the negative effects of improper posture and promote better health practices for individuals who spend prolonged periods sitting.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Framework for Reliable Sri Lankan Currency Authentication and Counterfeit Prevention
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Digital image processing plays a crucial role in enabling efficient and precise analysis, manipulation, and enhancement of images. In this study, researchers address challenges faced by individuals with visual impairments in recognizing currency denominations and identifying counterfeit banknotes. The researchers propose "Blind Trust," an IoT device that utilizes an Arduino Uno and a camera module to capture images of banknotes. To achieve these objectives, researchers utilize pre-processing techniques using the OpenCV and TensorFlow libraries to extract the notes/coins' characteristics. Custom datasets are developed for training Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models, which are then used to identify currency denominations and detect counterfeit currency. To enhance the model's performance, various preprocessing techniques are employed, resulting in high accuracy rates for both tasks. The currency notes identification model achieves an impressive 99% accuracy when tested on 25% of the data, while the currency coins identification model achieves 93% accuracy using InceptionV3. Additionally, the counterfeit currency detection model, created using VGG16, achieves an accuracy rate of 97% on a dataset comprising genuine and counterfeit currency images. Moreover, the note placement detection model attains 93% accuracy. "Blind Trust" holds great potential for enhancing financial security and accessibility for individuals with visual impairments. Its accuracy, speed, and ease of use contribute significantly to the development of new technologies aimed at improving their quality of life.

articleTitle: Utilizing AI and Data Analytics to Track Patterns and Attitudes of PUV Drivers on the Streets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Public utility vehicles (PUVs), such as buses and modern jeepneys, play a vital role in the transportation sector of the Philippines. They facilitate the connection of people and goods across the diverse islands of the country, fostering economic growth by granting access to essential services and bridging urban and rural areas. Nevertheless, accidents involving these public utility vehicles remain a significant concern. Hence, the focal point of this paper is to develop applications that enable the evaluation of roadworthiness and facilitate the enhancement of road competency and behavior among public utility vehicle drivers— effectively alleviating road accidents. This research paper discusses the development and integration of mobile applications, web applications, artificial intelligence, and data analytics to monitor and analyze drivers’ learning curves, driving patterns, and behaviors and assess the roadworthiness of public utility vehicle drivers. In partnership with the Department of Science and Technology and the Technological Institute of the Philippines, the project seeks to enhance drivers’ comprehension and actions by incorporating monitoring, assessment, and evaluation functionalities. To determine the profile of drivers who are frequently involved in accidents, receiving complaints, and obtaining violations, the Clustering Algorithm is implemented in the visualizations. On the other hand, the linear regression approach was used to determine the connection between different items in datasets. Through the implementation of this project, public utility vehicle drivers can attain the essential expertise and information to reduce the likelihood of being engaged in road accidents. This, in turn, plays a role in fostering a safer and more effective transportation sector in the Philippines.

articleTitle: Comparison of One-Stage and Two-Stage Strategies of Machine Learning Model for Rock Art Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Tracing rock art documentation has traditionally relied on manual identification by field specialists, which can be laborious and expensive. Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in archaeology has introduced new possibilities for enhancing rock art research. ML, a sub-field of AI, focuses on training models using data. At the same time, Deep Learning (DL) advances this approach with Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). Although ML methods have proven helpful for structured datasets, their application to rock art research remains largely unexplored. Object detection, a critical task in computer vision, involves predicting object locations and classes in images. State-of-the-art object detectors include two-stage detectors like Faster R-CNN and Mask R-CNN, which generate region proposals for classification and bounding-box regression, achieving high accuracy at the expense of speed. Conversely, one-stage detectors like YOLO treat object detection as a regression problem, sacrificing some accuracy for improved speed. Striking a balance between accuracy and speed poses a challenge in rock art research. In this context, a promising approach involves training a deep neural network to regress the difficulty scores produced by human annotators. An experiment was conducted using both one-stage and two-stage detectors on large-scale rock art images. The study presents the results and reflects their implications for rock art research. The findings emphasize the potential of AI, ML, and advanced computer vision techniques to revolutionize the field of rock art research, offering enhanced capabilities for analyzing, preserving, and interpreting these invaluable archaeological artifacts. Through automation of the detecting process and a decrease in the need for manual labor, these technologies can increase efficiency and accuracy in rock art studies.

articleTitle: Designing a Low Cost and Scalable Vehicle Rear-End Collision Warning System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: In most recent car models, the collision avoidance mechanism is installed in the car such as Auto Braking System. This built-in technology uses sensor installed in the car to provide auto stopping mechanism for the car. This system is very useful when the car is on a certain distance range with the front car. However, the technology offered pays less attention to another situation where the front car is out of sensing range. In highways, sometimes a driver in a speeding car has problem estimating a very slow or stalled traffic ahead. When the situation happens, the speeding car is forced to have a sudden drop of speed that increases the chance of collision. If the distance between the rear and front car is less than the minimum safe distance, a collision is likely to happen. To solve this, we proposed a protocol to trigger an alarm system vehicle rear-end collision warning system in mobile application. This protocol applies an existing mathematical model to calculate safe speed and distance relationship as a threshold to trigger the warning system. We present an algorithm structure that can be programmed in a smartphone application for drivers safety upon entering a risky threshold. Since this protocol is to be applied in mobile phone applications, the minimal cost for collision avoidance system in high traffic highways and regardless of the type of vehicles as well its advancement in technology.

articleTitle: Comparison of Stochastic Steepest Gradient Descent and Extended Kalman Filter as ARMA-FNN Learning Algorithms for Data-Driven System Identification of Batch Distillation Column
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: A process that is almost always present in the chemical industry is distillation. The plant used in this study is a batch-type distillation column system located in the ITB Honeywell Control Systems Laboratory, capable of separating binary mixtures of ethanol and water. To apply the control scheme effectively, the plant’s dynamics model is required. However, the challenge lies in the fact that the distillation column plant is a highly nonlinear and multivariable system based on its physical laws, with a limited number of sensors available to collect all states information, where only 1 state, which is also an output, can be measured. As a result, this research performs data-driven system identification through black-box modeling based on experimental input-output data using a neural network to generate a linear model. This research employs a discrete-time ARMA-FNN linear model for online identification of the distillation column system, with a focus on comparing learning algorithms for weight updating in the FNN. Specifically, a comparison is made between the stochastic Steepest Gradient Descent (SGD) algorithm and the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm. Both algorithms are suitable for comparison because they both operate in an instance-by-instance mode and can be employed for online system identification. Based on the results presented in TABLE II, it can be observed that the best Mean Squared Error (MSE) is achieved by entry number 2, utilizing the EKF algorithm, with a value of 5,5418e-05. Furthermore, as shown in TABLE II, entry number 3 demonstrates that the EKF algorithm can converge the fastest, approximately by the $6^{\mathrm{t}\mathrm{h}}$ instance. This achievement comes with a trade-off, as the resulting MSE slightly deteriorates.

articleTitle: Academic Stress of Students in Higher Education using Machine Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Academic stress results from greater academic demands and non-academic factors, resulting in students’ performance decline and their ability to cope with academic activities. For past years, academic stress studies have been expanding to provide a greater understanding of the factors contributing to stress, interventions, and support to reduce the chance of impacting students’ learning. At this point, this paper presents a systematic literature review of the academic stress of students in higher education based on machine learning techniques. As such, this paper presents the factors, data preparation, model development, performance, and general description of academic stress based on machine learning techniques. Thus, this paper expands the current understanding of academic stress and recommendations for future work.

articleTitle: Structured Trajectories for SLAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Many mobile robots generate unstructured trajectories and subsume seemingly random motion during SLAM. An extension to the SLAM problem is therefore considered to counter this. It is referred to as SLAM+CPP: Simultaneous, Localization, Mapping Plus Coverage Path Planning in which a robot is required to perform traditional SLAM but with a systematic pattern of movement such that the entire floor surface is traversed (coverage planning is performed) and mapped with structured and well-defined trajectories. This paper gives theoretical foundations and discusses challenges and whether solutions are available and gives results of basic studies that we have performed. A candidate solution is suggested that performs to expectations in simple single-room environments.

articleTitle: Wearable Foot Sensors for Detection and Tracking Epilepsy Seizure Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Monitoring patients’ vital signs is crucial in managing their epileptic seizure condition. However, traditional measuring devices can pose several limitations. This research aims to address these limitations by using a smart patch placed on the sole of the patient’s foot to measure critical vital signs such as peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), heart rate, body temperature, and photoplethysmography (PPG) signal, as well as tracking body position. This wireless patch allows patients to move freely, unlike traditional methods where data is transmitted through wires, which can limit patient mobility. Moreover, healthcare professionals can monitor a group of patients simultaneously without the need to be physically present at their location, which is typically required in conventional methods. The device provides two modes of information display-on-screen and audible, where the readings are spoken aloud in clear English and displayed on the screen, enabling real-time tracking of changes in vital signs. The device’s accuracy was evaluated by testing it on a sample of 20 patients, where it demonstrated a high accuracy of readings up to 99.62%.

articleTitle: Examination the Impact of Interactive Animation on College Students’ Behavior: Insights from TAM and SEM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Interaction in animation provides an immersive experience while also influencing user behaviour and acceptance, and interactive animation incorporating usability principles can further enrich the user experience. The research gap lies in understanding usability principles, immersion’s influence on user perception, and acceptance behavior of interactive animation. This study aims to explore the potential impact of aesthetic design and user control on viewers’ perceptions and to explore the mediating roles of immersion and positive emotions in shaping viewers’ behavioral intentions. A total of 117 university students participated in this survey, which was distributed to students via a self-administered questionnaire. Structural equation modelling analysis was carried out using R studio to define latent and observed variable relationships, parameter, estimation and assessment of goodness of fit, and the model was validated. The analysis revealed that the constructs of aesthetic design and user control have a significant impact on perception and immersion, which ultimately affects viewers’ behavioural intentions towards animation. The results of this study lay the foundation for the validation and extension of immersion theory and technology acceptance models in the field of animation. This study supports animation theory and technology model validation, enhancing user behavior experience understanding for animation design.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Fault Diagnosis in Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: The distribution network links the customer to the power supplier in power systems. One fundamental responsibility of the distribution network is to provide consumers with high-quality and reliable electricity. Faults in distribution grids cause severe burdens and introduce financial losses to the customers relying on them. The uncertainty about the location and the type of fault amplifies the issue as it complicates the maintenance process and causes additional losses. This paper used the short-time Fourier transform to extract features from a simulated active distribution network’s measurements. The features extracted were then fed to feedforward neural network models, which we trained for fault detection, classification, and localization. Results demonstrate that the developed models accurately detect and classify the faults in the active distribution network, demonstrating the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed models. Also, the proposed approaches were able to locate the faults in the simulated network accurately. Eventually, suggested models could elegantly handle load variation, renewable energy resources generation, and fault information ambiguity.

articleTitle: Development of a Small- Scale Material Handling Machine for an Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 13th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)
abstract: Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (ASRS) are used in various industries and applications. In particular, small-scale ASRS systems offer several advantages in terms of efficiency, space utilization, and labor savings. Some applications of small-scale ASRS are retail and E-commerce Warehousing, pharmaceutical and healthcare, food and beverage industry, pharmacies, electronics manufacturing, cold storage facilities, libraries, and agriculture. Learning about automation technology in higher education is of paramount importance in preparing graduates for the workforce. This learning often faces challenges due to limited access and affordability of practice instruments. Conventional ASRS solutions are often expensive and impractical for educational purposes.
